(Page 11)
Recommend to ages 17yrs and up does have swearing, sex, and may not like how some people are called in this book but are treated kindly.. Gina Clabo

I'm having a bit of a hard time really processing all of my thoughts on this book. This isn't just a genre novel. And don't get me wrong, I love genre novels but that just isn't what this is. This is true literature that happens to contain zombies. This is not really anything I anticipated in what I thought this book would contain.

Temple is such a wonderful heroine to follow and love in this. The awful things she's seen and had to do really changed her in her short years. Her perspective is so stunning and optimistic for the state of the world. Her understanding of god as a 'slick god' was so interesting especially to see how she interpreted the world she's in. Her life has been so difficult but she doesn't remain bitter and continues to find beauty. I found her unique perspective on the slugs (aka zombies) to be so interesting and her morals in this world.

The main plot point of the novel accomplishes something that I feel The Walking Dead has been trying to cover and just doesn't fully get there. What is the value of human life in this world? How does this world cause you to change? If you don't stick to your morals, what else do you have left?

There were some world building aspects that I found to be a bit unrealistic but that never removed me from the book and doesn't take away from how great the writing is. I wish I bought this book instead of reading it through my library. Alden Bell deserves all the money.

One of the best zombie books I've ever read. I read this literally in two nights and didn't go to sleep on the last night until my eyes were burning from staying open, and my heart was racing from the suspense of my favorite character as she paraded, gurkha in hand, slaying all the monsters she came across. It is such a brilliant novel for being such a short book, you will fall into it and not want to crawl out of the dark, dreary world. The author writes with such clarity and unforgiving nature that you can feel, taste, smell every bit of the scenery and the characters you can see them in the back of your mind clear as day.

Temple is one not to be forgotten, she is a spitfire of a girl and a warrior. She is the heroine of the story and is looking for a way to survive among the wasteland of the undead and the wretched. She has alot of blood on her heart, but it's in the right place. She knows how to swing that gurkha blade down on all who jest against her mission and she is not afraid of anyone or any monster. No matter how big. No matter how viie. She just does what she knows best. Living.

You'll fall in love with her and the slow boy she picks up along the road. It's not a easy trail for them. They encounter alot of baddies excluding all the gross slugs that want their meat. It's definitely a swirly rabbit hole of a book, it will trap you and entrance you in it's creative solemnity. I already want to read it again lol.

I rate this somewhere between a 3.5 and a 4.

This book is not without its weaknesses. The post zombie world doesn't always ring true. The zombies themselves seem to be seriously underpowered; they don't ever serve as a meaningful threat and it isn't clear how they came to take over large parts of North America. For example in the first chapter the protagonist (a 15 year old girl) is ambushed by 3 zombies in a cramped basement. She dispatches them with a knife and her bare hands without much difficulty. She later kills a dozen of them in about 2 minutes with a rifle. Throughout the book people are shown very easily dispatching the zombies, who seem to mostly shuffle around aimlessly waiting to get killed. One would think that clearing out all the zombies would be a pretty easy task for the military, or even a decent police force.

It also seems strange how much of the electricity grid is still operating (who is maintaining the lines and the generating stations?) and how easy it seems to be to find food and gasoline just lying around.

But for all that the book really is quite engaging - it really draws you in. A flawed but very likeable protagonist. A menacing (non-zombie) antagonist (though I'm not sure I understood or bought his motivations). Just the right length. Sly humor throughout. And it has some really great passages describing the post apocalyptic world - reminded me of McCarthy's Blood Meridian in many places.

Definitely worth a read.

Plot:
Zombies have infested a fallen America. A young girl named Temple is on the run. Haunted by her past and pursued by a killer, Temple is surrounded by death and danger, hoping to be set free.For twenty-five years, civilization has survived in meager enclaves, guarded against a plague of the dead. Temple wanders this blighted landscape, keeping to herself and keeping her demons inside her heart. She can't remember a time before the zombies, but she does remember an old man who took her in and the younger brother she cared for until the tragedy that set her on a personal journey toward redemption. Moving back and forth between the insulated remnants of society and the brutal frontier beyond, Temple must decide where ultimately to make a home and find the salvation she seeks.

My Thoughts
This book surprised me. The cover doesn't intrigue me to pick it up, and I don't typically read zombie books. But, this book is a solid novel. The main character, Temple, and the main villain Moses are written very well, and both characters are easy to like. The journey is a solid journey, and the ending, although not the ending I wanted, is good. I think that in an apocalypse, everyone dies eventually, and that shows you never know when you will go.

I really wanted the ending to be Moses vs. Temple in a big showdown, and whoever wins, wins. But that was stolen from me by the Damn Mutant girl, who I thought was going to be only in a chapter. But it is whatever.
