Poetic and haunting, this one will stick with you for a while, and if they taught it in English class, more kids might like reading. They wouldn't sleep very well, of course, but who needs sleep?

If Cormac McCarthy was really, really into playing Fallout 3 to the extent that he decided to pen a novel about a young girl hacking up zombies and mutants while trudging through a futuristic, post-apocalyptic America, this would be that book. Also, Cormac McCarthy would be the coolest 80-year old ever.

The Reapers are the Angels contains some beautifully written, evocative and unpredictable stuff and it's a shame that the companion novel, Exit Kingdom, had such a limited release.

Something new and deeply absorbing about this post-apocalyptic zombie story. It's interesting to see something not set in the immediate aftermath of the outbreak. I love the sense of purpose to the story, and the feeling that it's always going somewhere and never just floundering. The writing is beautiful, and it really captures the post-apocalyptic evolution of language. Just loved it, very readable.

This was more of a 2.5 star book for me. I think I just had the wrong expectations going into this book. This book is about a girl who is aimlessly traveling and makes the wrong guy angry. She ends up on the run from him as he chases her across the country trying to kill her. I really didn’t like any of the characters in the book and the world didn’t seem too disjoined for my taste. Oh, yeah and there are zombies.

This is a brutal and beautiful book about human nature, faith, hope and pain. It's disguised as a zombie apocalypse horror novel, and the main character is a 15 year old girl. Don't let this fool you! It's much more than "just" horror fiction, and I wouldn't classify it as YA, either. Zombies are definitely a constant and present threat, but they aren't the only monsters in this world. They're just the only undead ones.

I like a good zombie book. Unfortunately so many are disappointing. This one however was anything but. It was unique in its own way, as unique as you can expect any story about zombies to be. I loved the ending. I enjoyed the characters. I don't think I will read anymore in the series however, mostly for fear that anymore could just lead to disappointment. I think this book on its own is perfect.

Some of the grammatical errors and choices seemed a literary trick to make the book more trendy. The dialogue was hard to follow, as if the characters all had magical telepathy. The world building was a bit weak. Too many unanswered questions, like how did they still have power, coke and stocked convenience stores 25 years after the zombies started munching on the population. I did connect with Temple, but hated how her story ended.

Yes, this is a book with zombies, a post apocalyptic tale set about twenty-give years after the world is overrun by zombies. Yes, of course, that means there is the obligatory blood and gore and split heads. But there is so much more to this than all of that. Strange as it might seem, this story also contains much beauty, and Temple, the fifteen year old heroine is a remarkable character. This book really touched me.

Excellent character study. A good read. You don't have to like zombies to like this book. In fact, if you like zombie books, you might have some qualms about them taking an elevator in a building in the middle of nowhere. If you're going to write an apocalyptic novel, you should get the survival details right. But, still, an excellent novel, better character development than your average zombie novel.

Coming of Age, Zombies (not the main focus), 25 years post apocalypse, Macabre, Dark, Survival, Inner conflict, Character driven, Intensifying, Southern Gothic, Psychological Suspense

Some parts I found a bit unbelievable, but overall kept me interested and on the edge of my seat. Great crossover for YA as Temple is 15 in the book, but more stylistically complex than typical YA. Read alike for The Road. Not very hopeful, don't read on vacation.

Wow, I absolutely loved this book. I loved the way it was written and I loved Temple. If you are looking for an action Zombie book then this isn't really the book for that even though it does take place in a Zombie apocaliptic world. The story is much deeper than that and Temple although young in body is old in soul. I can't say enough good things about her story other than give this book a try, you won't be disappointed.

This was amazing. I can't stop thinking about it, and it's going to stay with me for a long time. It's a zombie book, but the zombies aren't the main characters here. They're sort of off-stage. The end of the world has come and gone. The zombies show up now and then, but this is really about the life of the girl Temple, and her relationships with the people she meets on the road. I'll never forget her, or Maury or Moses. So wonderful.

4.5 stars. I really enjoyed this book, even though I struggled a bit with the style in the beginning. I would have preferred quotation marks for speech or something at least. (The style is frequently compared to Cormac McCarthy, and I have never been able to finish one of his books.) While this book is not a gore fest, parts of it were terrifying to me. I liked Temple's kindness, and I even liked the character of Moses Todd. I'm unsure how I feel about the ending.

Wow. This was a beautifully written book set 25 years into a zombie apocalypse. The main character is unique and flawed and very much a product of her environment, with a distinct (if dialecty) voice. I loved the prose, which did get pretty far up its own ass in places, but I've been reading a lot of Thomas Harris lately, so it didn't feel out of place. High recommended for people who think they might like to read The Road, but like their books about two shades less grimdark.

It's overall a very awsome book I feel like I'm actually in a post apocalyptic situation having to survive with just my wits ant the tools I have and its over all very emotional and heart breaking at some parts even. The book itself seem interesting enough to read again which I did and it was even better the second time. Reapers are the Angeles is one of those books where you just can't put it down I would recommend this book to everyone who can handle a good horror story.

Quick read. Although set in a post zombie apocalyptic America, the zombies do not take center stage but are just props adding depth to the characters. The style in which it is written, the atmosphere, and the imagery Bell is able to conjure up, reminds me of novels I was assigned to read for summer reading lists in school. I enjoyed this book and it brings about many emotions from hope all the way through to it's disheartening core.

A very strong female lead character, wise beyond her years as one would be born into a zombie apocalypse. There is a road trip and once again we find that humans are more dangerous than zombies. Toward the end of her journey she becomes less jaded and more introspective, there is a sense of weariness about her as though she has lived a thousand years in her short 16. And yes, I shed a tear at the end, I think my first zombie reading tear.

Although it took me a while to read the first few chapters, afterwards I could not put it down. Brilliant writing, a story that builds up never lets go. I actually felt a little depressed at times, but then in the world where Temple lives, there are no happy endings and tragedy has to be survived by moving forward without guilt. Absolutely recommend it to anyone who wants to read something human and different

Obviously I didn't get this book as there are a lot of good reviews about it.
This is the story of Temple, a 15 year old girl that has grown up in a post apocalyptic world dominated by zombies.
She kills a man that tries to attack her and his brother then hunts her down to extract vengeance.
I found the descriptions too wordy and for the majority of the novel they didn't help me picture what it was they were describing. And I didn't like the story and I hated the end. Enough said!

Very solid "meh". I think this falls under the category of "My expectations were too high", so the book disappointed. I was expecting a twist, or crazy exciting ending, but got neither. Meh. It would have been better with more scary zombies and less jaw jabbin. Also, I think the reader of the book on tape may have lessened my interest in this book. She was surely no Jim Dale. Wouldn't recommend, 3.5/10

I'm usually unable to look past some of the issues I felt this book had (illogical pacing, unreasonable scenarios, baffling timing, rejected realism) - - but the strengths outweigh the weaknesses, and frankly hide them in some really sweet smoke and mirror business that I don't care to look at too closely.
It's not the best zombie book you're going to read - - but it is easily better than 85% or more of them.
I won't reread it - but I liked it and was happy to turn the pages.

Interesting. Still processing my feelings on this one. One of the blurbs on the back said something to the effect of if Flannery O'Connor wrote a zombie novel. I don't really agree with that as there is significantly less humor in this than in O'Connor. It could be lumped into the Southern Gothic I suppose. It really, though, reminds me of Mary Doria Russell's The Sparrow. It sort of has that spiritually devastating effect that lingers after you've finished reading.

Everything was so amazing about this book except Temple's death. ****, I really wish she could've atleast seen Niagara falls before her death. Pathetic, so so pathetic.And what was that end anyway ???!! She was buried under a gravestone named "Sarah Mary Williams", thats not even her real name !! Now nobody can really know what happened to her ..... My heart aches for her coz i really liked her personality and she doesn't deserve a death like THAT !!

This is another that didn't get good until the very, very end. The dynamic between Temple & Moses, at first typical, became something a bit more intriguing. I would've liked to see the story played out an it further, but then this wouldn't have been as good as it ended up being. Totally made up for the lack of quotation marks, but on the other side of the book, I can see how that stylistic choice made sense in a world very far beyond the rules of conventional English.

Didn't really care for this book all that much. In my opinion, the main character Temple was not likable and the story line was weak. I guess maybe I am used to master writers when it comes to the subject of zombies...and this one, fell way short. It is a quick read, took me a little over 2 days. Only thing I took from it were the tags "meatskin" and "slugs".

I am not a fan of apocalyptic fiction. This book started painfully slow and very sparse on the descriptions. There is a 15 or 16 year old girl that is in a constant fight for survival in a world fuel of zombies. You come to realize that her fight is not only against the monsters but her own past. This book might be popular with Zombies or End of the world story lovers but it did not do it for me.

It is rare i begin a book and finish it within 24 hours - my lifestyle is prohibitive. The Reapers are the Angels made the cut - reading it within 24 hours - hiding in bathrooms, bedrooms and pick-up trucks; taking longer than usual to run errands - I just finished it.

and i sit, this morning, waiting for my breath to return.....more later...

A very different kind of Zombie novel. Yes, the world is full of flesh eaters, but they are but a backdrop to the real story here. It's the travels & story of Temple that grabs you & reels you in. I got to admit that the mutants were a nice touch and I was glad to see Bell not sell out to a feel good ending. This story has great pacing & was an enjoyable read.

This book is one of those rare finds: the literary horror novel. Beautiful sentences, a unique style and voice, a main character who both delights and infuriates--and a story which pulls no punches. I predict this will be nominated for and win a number of prizes in its genre. A real fucking delight.

More of a 3.5. A quick go, but it's a Zombie Lite read as they are very secondary. Which is ok because this book has several strong well described characters. If a Zombie writer married an English Lit writer then their child would write this novel. It was fun, and a bit thought provoking. I think I'd like to dissect it in a classroom more then shivering in my biik reading corner.

I forgot about reading this book until I came across it again on my update page. From what I remember it just didn't do much for me. I seem to have bad luck with books lately. Particularly with books I've been hearing lots of good things about. It just didn't really grab me. I kept picking this up and putting it down and I was just barely getting into it. I had to eventually just give up on it.

This book was interesting, and the writing style was pretty good. It reminded me of The Road in a lot of ways, only not quite that good and there were zombies. The interesting thing about this novel was that the zombies were too slow and stupid to be much of a threat, they were more just a fact of life. It was the other living people who were the biggest threat.

I really don't know what to say about this book. This is the 1st book I have read about vampires -I enjoyed the book to a point. It was very confusing as to what was going on - took awhile to get into it. In the end the interplay between Temple, Maury and Moses was good. Now that I have gotten through the 1st 1 like this I am looking forward to reading others.

I really enjoyed this one. Another apocalyptic story. I liked the way this was formatted and the epic adventure of it all.
The ending was a bit drab, and there were parts that dragged a little, but overall, I enjoyed it.
It is one of those books that sticks with you and makes you think about it after you finish it.

I really enjoyed this! I went to a bookstore and it was on the "New Releases" section, and I thought the cover/title looked cool so I decided to get it. It was actually really good...it got a bit slow in the middle, but then in the end it got better. It's really short as well...so if you have nothing else to read you could finish this in a few days!

I am unashamed of reading this teen lit. book. Quick read, good prose, stream-of-consciousness, gritty, and deals with some pretty heavy topics and concepts of mortality, life, and death without really taking a stance on the meaning of life or what death is. Felt a little preachy at times, though, but I forgave it.

There was a weird side track in the middle of the book, but otherwise I really enjoyed this book and read it rather quickly. You really don't have to be into zombies to enjoy this book, because they weren't really a threat to the characters. More like a detail in the background. All in all a good read with a main character who is a hoot to read.

The writing style of this book wasn't bad at all. It was an easy read. My problem was that I just didn't care for the main character. I'm not the type of person that needs to identify with a character to enjoy a book, but I do want to be able to like them just a little. I also felt there was something missing, but I can't figure out what that is. It just wasn't a book for me.

The Reapers Are the Angels was one of the 2011 winners of the Alex Award, an award given to ten books written for adults that have special appeal to young adults, ages 12 through 18. Place a hold on this book and pick it up at one of the Chemung County Library District Branches!

In a time where post-apocalyptic fiction is starting to take off (maybe because of the economy?), I find myself drawn to what would happen if we had to start over...and this book involves "zombie" characters, my worst nightmare. The book was quick and easy. Wasn't a happy ending I hoped for, but really is that life? Definitely worth the few hours :)

Temple, a fifteen year old girl wandering the wastelands of the south filled with undead. she comes across varies communities and other wanderers trying to survive. The book kept me interested from page one i think because Temple comes across so many others trying to survive. The undead are described as 'slugs' who are physically slow, so Temples main advisary is another survivor.

This was amazing. Really, really amazing. You forget, sometimes, that when you have a zombie novel you don't have to sacrifice amazing character-driven plots. This did both. And it was amazing. Close, close third person done well, strong female character, etc., etc. ...what more could I want?

Though I'm only 3/4 of the way through, this horrific little novel is surprisingly good! One of those books you can't wait to get back to, not only because the story is an excellent twist on the current zombie genre, but it's poetic and well written. It's like literary horror...which isn't even a genre yet, but def should be!

Temple is by far one of the most kick ass young heroines and so fully fleshed out that I wanted to look up her telephone number and ask her out for drinks.

And this is the only book that was so lyrical I wished I had heard it and NOT just read it.

The ending was the only facet of this book that tripped me up a bit, other than that this book kicks ass!!!

Unusual story that follows a girl who has grown up never knowing the world before the zombie apocalypse. Meditations on good and evil and how people react when their world is turned upside down are powerfully moving. The book ends, even in the midst of such bleak despair, on a hopeful note, like The Road by Cormac McCarthy.

A fantastic novel. much more than a 'zombie' novel.It is also much more than a apocalpse novel. It is a story of Temple, a young girl who has to survive on the road. A girl who has to live with her decisions right or wrong. The reader feels like they are walking next to Temple and experiencing her travels.

So beautiful. It left a burning hole in my heart. It left me to think deep stuff. This is one of those books where my tears just shed on its own. I love the experience of reading this book. I'd learn to admire Temple and her thoughts in a world where enigma, gone crazy and lonesome are an understatement. So worth it!

This is a very enjoyable read. I liked the tight, well focused, story. A little YA for me but still very good. It tells the story of a young girl lost in a harsh world fighting her demons and to stay alive. It's the type of read that on the outside is almost silly, but on the inside stays with you for a long time. Tight, simple, and enjoyable.

This is the zombie novel as literature. Gorgeous passages throughout a story told in an altogether refreshing manner. This is not for the faint of heart as it is pretty gory and violent all over. Temple is great heroine and the story is compelling. I just felt emptier than I should have when it was over. 3.5 really. I think I just expected...more.

Perhaps one of the best "literary" zombie novels. It's a mix between Huck Finn & George Romero. The idea of setting a zombie novel 25 years after the outbreak is brilliant. The language used reminds me of Deadwood, because of the ornateness uses. The only writer working today whose style is similar is James Lee Burke.For me this was more enjoyable than Zone One. Heartily recommend it.

Not your average zombie novel. Our 15 year old heroine, Temple was born after the zombie plague into a world that barely retains any remnants of civilization. Fleeing the psychotic brother of a man she killed she embarks on a road trip. Horrifying, heartbreaking and beautifully written, this book is one that will stay with you.

This book is so beautifully and thoughtfully written, it is almost incidentally a zombie novel, although of course there are some gruesome or horrifying passages. But it's more a novel of a journey, both physical and spiritual, with a southern gothic style. I am so happy to have stumbled across this book.

I absolutely love this book. In a world where everyone sees only darkness and despair the young protagonist sees beauty and purpose. The fact that it's a terrifying beauty and a horrible purpose doesn't matter. The world is as it is, and she does what is necessary to survive in it.

The story follows this girl and the man who has sworn to kill her across a broken America.

I really liked this book (especially since I just randomly picked it up at the library). Another zombie book, but with some differences, zombies are slow moving, so it seems like more people survived. Characters all very interesting and kept your interest. Some God talk, but wasn't too bothersome.

Beautifully written. Yes, I know its a zombie book and that the two don't seem to go together. But this book is the exception. This is a book about survival in the worst of conditions. Its haunting and full of sadness and leaves you longing for a better life for poor Temple. What will ever happen to helpless and dependent Maury{and how on earth has he survived for so long}?

Great book. Very reminiscent of Faulkner and Cormac McCarthy. The language and imagery are wonderful and terrible, beautiful and awful. An excellent and enjoyable read, even if you don't like zombies. If you enjoy this style, I recommend books by Carson McCullers, William Faulkner, and Cormac McCarthy.

The ending of this book will linger with you for a while. This is an intense read, with eccentric characters, set in post-apocaplytic USA. The intensity of the book reminded me of how I felt watching the Coen brothers movie, No Country for Old Men: on the edge of my seat, fingers gripped into the chair, breathless. Highly recommended.

The one word I would use to describe this book is meditative... at least as meditative a book about a zombie apocalypse can be. Our protagonist, Temple, is a 15 year old girl in a zombie infested wasteland, and has never known anything but. I loved that this book comments more on the living, and what it really means to be alive.

Even though there are some pretty glaring logic mistakes given that it's supposed to take place 25 years after zombie apocalypse--and even though I don't approve of not using quotation marks!!!--, this is a great book. Thank goodness there's still some good zombie stories coming out amongst the trash.

This book was an Alex Award nomine, an award for Young Adult novels. However, this book is well outside the scope of a Young Adult novel. Other than e main character being a 15 year old girl, this book can be enjoyed by anyone who enjoys Southern Gothic or even Cormac McCarthy. Definitely recommended.

This is a good one. It's one of those books that touches you unexpectedly. It's captivating and heartbreaking and wondrous. I loved it.
*note: there is a very important scene in the book that takes place in Tulsa! fun to see our little place on Earth written so well in such a great book. made me smile :)

I really enjoyed this story. It's about a young girl trying to survive on her own in a post apocalyptic zombie world. She struggles not only with the physical threat of being eaten alive every day, but also with the social struggles of trying to live with other humans in a lawless world. I really disliked how the author chose to end this novel, but I would still highly recommend this book.

Who knew that a story about zombies could be so poetic? Bell writes a lyrical story about life after the apocalypse viewed through the eyes of a 15-year old nomad haunted by things past. There are monsters and then there are Monsters, you might be surprised at which is which. The Reapers Are the Angels is gorgeous, creepy, and has a surprise ending that I never saw coming.

Finished "The Reapers Are the Angels" by Alden Bell. Another well-written zombie book, this one about a young girl making her way in the post-apocalyptic world. With vivid descriptions and colorful characters, I recommend this one even if zombie-fiction isn't your thing. (I wouldn't say it's my thing, but this is the third zombie book in recent memory for me.)

I never would have thought I would be so taken in by a zombie book with a teenage heroine. But this book is so much more than that, and will probably stick with me for a long time. Other reviewers have done an excellent job of explaining how beautiful and messy and philosophical and amazing this book is, so I'll just say that for me personally, I am so glad I read this.

This was Amy's pick for SDBBE. As with all of Amy's books it' was something I wouldn't have chosen to read on my own. It was about zombies and what the world was like with zombies on it. You follow a girl, Temple, as she moves through the world. She is really positive towards God and others even though the world she lives in is so ugly. It was good and I'm glad I read it.

3.5 stars

So, zombies took over the world 25 years ago and civilisation crumbled but you can still get gas from gas stations, merry-go-rounds are still going around by themselves etc. etc. These were the instances where I put it down and said "What?!" Other than those ridiculous parts, I really liked the actual story.

I can't quite explain why I liked this book so much. It's not brilliantly written, it's quite violent, and the characters are mostly mean. It is a better zombie book than most...maybe because the zombies are not the central focus of the book and most of the conflict is with the aforementioned mean (but kinda complex) people.

Just finished reading THE REAPERS ARE THE ANGELS by Alden Bell. It's a post-zombie apocalypse story about a girl who travels between pockets of surviving humanity. Bell succeeds at using the ZA as a symbolic backdrop without having the story become morally heavy-handed --- and without losing the excitement and "fun" of killin' zombies. Good job, Mr. Bell. Good job.

An absolutely fantastic read.

This is a literary fiction take on the zompocalypse, seen through the lens of a sixteen year old girl. Temple, as she's known, is an excellent protagonist, and her struggle to survive in the wasteland is truly gripping.

I've read a metric ton of zombie fiction, and I can tell you that without a doubt this is one of my top 5 books on the subject.

Wasn't a fan. It felt like it was written to be a formulaic hollywood movie. The writing was really self conscious and felt weighed down in trying to produce some sort of beautiful poetic ugliness. Neither the story nor the writing style ever felt as unexpected or original as the book seemed to think it was.

A book for those who spend their lives traveling and seeking, who see the miracles in everyday things, and who know that good can't exist without evil. It's a notable surprise that a book about a zombie-infested future could be written so beautifully, so vividly, and so poignantly. As soon as I reached the last word, I wanted to cry, and then immediately read it again.

Un livre vraiment poignant ! Je crois que ça fait longtemps que j'avais pas eu aussi peur et que je n'avais pas étais aussi triste en lisant un livre.

Temple est vraiment attachante, on ne peut que s'identifier à elle. Elle est perdu dans ce monde déchu et fait tout pour survivre tout en essayant de ne pas se trahir.

Une magnifique lecture qui m'a tiré quelques larmes.

I enjoyed this very much I was quite surprised with the ending. It is difficult for me to put into words how I feel about this book or even how I feel about Temple I have yet to come across a heroin such as her. I feel very deeply about this character, very fond of her. Any thing else words escape me.

The reader Tai Simmons did a superb job.

This is actually a good rating coming from me, someone who can't handle zombies. I didn't hate it! That's a good thing! I did feel that there could have been more, and that bad things that keep happening to the main character started to grate on me a little. She stays optimistic the whole time but seriously, <input type="checkbox" class="spoiler__control" aria-label="The following text has been marked spoiler. Toggle checkbox to reveal or hide." onchange="this.labels[0].setAttribute('aria-hidden', !this.checked);" id="e21e4fb0-0444-4dd0-8ce8-f7a079b7e091" /><label aria-hidden="true" class="spoiler" for="e21e4fb0-0444-4dd0-8ce8-f7a079b7e091">mutant zombie people</label> was a little much.

This was a a very surprising book. I started off for the first 50 or so pages thinking I would not like it and from then on read it with the expectation that it would be crap especially with the way in which Temple speaks. However as the book went on I found myself pleasantly surprised I grew quite attached to the characters. Good book worth reading.

I hadn't been able to get myself to read any of the popular zombie books everyone seems to love right now but I heard this one was well written so I gave it a shot. I'm very glad I did. Poetic and horrific at the same time, this book is darkly beautiful. It reminds me a lot of the The Road. If you liked The Road, you'll probably like this book.

This post-apocalyptic book not only deals with zombies, but also dabbles with spirituality and personal beliefs of the main character, Temple.

After the world is overrun by zombies, Temples wanders the land and does what is needed to survive. She has difficult choices to make, and I felt myself wondering what would happen next. Good book.

This is zombies, yes, but this is well-written, Southern Gothic, Cormac McCarthy-style zombies. This is one of the best books I have read in a while and it's about zombies. It is gruesome and dark, and doesn't have any fancy post-modern tricks up its sleeve. It is just pure good writing. About zombies.

At only 225 pages, it is a quick read. Honestly it only took me a couple of hours to read, but this may be because I couldn't put it down...it was that good! I absolutely fell in love with the main character Temple, a 15 year old teenager that is growing up during the Zombie Apocalypse, who quickly learns the necessary tools to survive including the need to kill or be killed.

"Infinities are warm places that never end. And they aren't about good and evil, they're just peaceful-like and calm, and they're where all travelers go eventually, and they are round everywhere you look because you can't have any edges in infinities. And also they make forever seem like an okay thing."

Exciting and thrilling book! I couldn't put the book down and when I did I wanted to read more. I loved how it told a story of a young girl trying to survive the dangerous life she was born into, not knowing what tomorrow holds but to keep on fighting for her life. There were a few things I didn't like about the book but I liked it for the most part

This is terrific as an adventure novel, as suspense, as literature. Layered, rich, and lovely writing that is full of surprises and beauty without distraction. Just go out and read it, already. It's not long, it's certainly not cheery (post zombie apocalypse, after all), but it's beautiful and satisfying.(less)

I wanted to like this much more than I did. I loved the writing style, and the idea, but the ending sucked. I don't want to spoil the story for anyone, but sometimes a bad ending is good! Sometimes a sad ending is necessary to the story, but this wasn't, it seemed like a sad ending for the sake of it, it brought nothing to the story and it made a good book into an average one.

The abundance of gone things, it'll bury you.

I highlighted lines and passages in this book like crazy. Like crazy! It was crazy how much certain things spoke to me. This should get optioned immediately; it would make a hell of a film. And Temple is one damn likeable young protagonist. It's more of a 4.5 star book for me, to be honest.

Finally read this book and absolutely loved it! We did an exercise in our "listening for the soul" group of looking for the holy in the ordinary moments of our days.
I'd say that this book captures this idea in how the young girl in a post-apocalypse zombie world has mastered this skill! Very dark story but somehow beautiful and hopeful.

Lyrical, intimate yet widescreen, bleak yet heartbreakingly beautiful, desperately sad but somehow hopeful, a central character, Temple, who is nuanced, clothed in shades of grey and red, empathetic yet terrifying. The zombie apocalypse has never come with such descriptive beauty, the image of the fish will stick with me for a long time. This is near perfection.

It was a decent read. It kept my attention, and I found the perspective of the protagonist to be interesting, if not entirely believable. There were times when the story and the writing were clunky, and the setting is fairly implausable, but it was alright. Nothing mind-blowing, and I'm unsure why it's gotten the hype that it's gotten, unless it's because of how the protagonist is written.

An intricate and intimate book examining the complexities of the human condition and the importance of the journey over the destination. With Zombies.

Read Katie's full review here

Very interesting read, especially since I just finished reading The Road. I wish there would have been more of the back story of how did we get to the current state of where the plot takes place. Temple is a strong, brave, character not to be reckoned with! Similar to The Road, I would not last a day in this world.

« L'illustration de la couverture représente très bien le contenu de ce récit. Un univers assez sombre où l'espoir n'a pas de place. Cependant, la plume d'Alden Bell est juste divine. Des zombies oui, mais pas que... Au bout du compte, une histoire poignante. » Lire ma chronique → http://bookmetiboux.blogspot.fr/2013/...

Una novela hermosa. El final realmente lo esperaba de otra manera y Alden Bell supo como darle un giro de lo más curioso con ese final que escribió. Temple termina por caerte bien y Maury logra sacar a flote tu preocupación, esa misma que Temple mostraba por él. Mosses Todd tampoco se queda atras.
Una excelente novela...

A fun read, but for someone who has read (too) many zombie/apocalypse/survival books there were a few things that just didn't make sense...the biggest being that electrical power and cars still worked 25 years after being abandoned. Still some interesting characters, a good pace and the ending was...well - I'll not spoil it.

The Road meets The Walking Dead. Written in McCarthy's minimalist style, humanity is front-and-center in this tale of a teen orphan's quest for love and beauty amidst a world of soulless "meatskins" (aka: zombies), and the savagery necessary to survive. The story's sparse, but the writing is, in places, transcendent. Really liked this!

The book was engaging and had a poetic element to it. It was unrealistic, not in the sense that it took place in a post-apocalyptic wasteland, but that the main character was a small, 16 year old girl who knew her way around a knife and could give any grown a run for their money in a fight. I would recommend this book.

Worst book ever. If you ever consider reading it, don't. I have never read anything that was this poorly written and with such lame and bad character description. The main character Temple did not make any sence what so ever, neither did anyone else, it felt like something a 12 year old could had written.

Don't read it. Just don't.

Am I the only one who has a problem with everyone having electricity and running water 25 years into the zombie apocalypse??? And Coke - have you ever had a soda that is even 3 years old? I have and it is disgusting! I can't even imagine enjoying a soda that is 25 years old and not immediately vomiting!

Those issues aside, this book is mostly enjoyable.

I really enjoyed this book. It was quite dark and not what I expected. The ending was AMAZING! didn't see that one coming. In my opinion, it was a well written book with amazing descriptions. I felt like the author transported me to that futuristic time. I don't agree with the author's vision of a post apocalyptic world. I would have envisioned it a bit differently. Overall, good read.

This book was truly unique and is not to be missed! If you're looking for a book that is exceedingly well written, features genuinely different and complex characters, is unpredictable, and just plain creepy then this book is the one for you. If you thing zombie books are overdone and overrated I challenge you to read this one. Temple our mc was simply brilliant and one helluva female heroine.

If Cormac Mccarthy had a love child with a zombie, this would be the book. Not very good. It felt like I was reading Cliff Notes instead of a book. Very dry overly wrought prose and as always when a writer needs to show their "talent", no quotation marks with dialogue. Better out there, skip this one.

actual rating 4.5
this was a very intriguing novel and not at all what I expected it to be like. Instead of action pack zombie gore I got a soul deep view of the human condition. Its a tale of survival, life, regret, and guilt. And let me tell you that Alden Bell certainly has a way with words as he has managed to weave a very intricate novel that goes deeper than the average zombie apocalypse.

sinceramente el ppio lento, de modo que puedas conocer el caracter de nuestra protagonista y el por que de él.Asi que no desespereis porque todo lo que sigue es alucinante. Y el final bueno es uno de esos que te deja impactado. A tener en cuenta que esta narrado en 3 persona y eso hasta que te
acostumbras es un poco rollo.

Great book, beautifully written and it had a great ending scene. It also felt too short. I would have loved to have seen more background/character exploration on a lot of the characters Temple meets such as Moses, Ruby, Lee, Maury, etc. If you like the movies I am Legend or Book of Eli this would be a great read.

Great book, but short. Very interesting writing style. Stance that there is no quotes to indicate when people are talking which I found a bit jarring. Besides that though, a great zombie story. I read it cuz it was listed the #1 book of the top 10 zombie books zombie lovers must read. And now I'm starting the #3 book on that top ten list, Raising Stony May all.

I enjoyed some of the prose, but the situations were a bit unbelievable (like electricity and working gas stations and diesel engine trains 25 years after a zombie apocalypse), and the main character's voice was much older than her stated 15 years. I don't think I'll be picking up the next in the series.

C'était correct, mais sans plus. Une histoire avec une jeune fille brillante et courageuse qui combat les zombies. Il y a certain très bon passage qui font réfléchir, mais j'ai eu de la misère à m'attacher aux personnages. C'était un bon livre pour un roman que j'ai choisi à l'aveuglette, au hasard!

Okay, I'm not really sure what rating to give this book. I was enjoying it up until the devastating ending. I could not get past the ending. It was well-written, definitely meditative take on zombie land with really interesting characters. But man, the ending. Not entirely sure I'd recommend the book, but glad I read it?

Reads like Cormac McCarthy fan fiction. Bad Cormac McCarthy fan fiction. Nothing that the Romero films or any other work of Zombie-fiction hasn't done already. Also, the author seems to be unaware of the fact that electricity and Diesel fuel are industrial products actual people have to actually work for.

Zombies. But wait, the story isn’t really about zombies. The term isn’t even used until several chapters in. Temple, a young woman with brutal knife skills, navigates the desolate plane of zombies and humans who devour each other. A few of the scenes make me squeamish, but the characters absolutely fascinated me by surviving in bare, violent, and tumultuous circumstances.

This book was gritty, realistic and surprisingly pleasant to read, with unique takes on a familiar genre. It's just....wow.

One less star because I disagreed with the ending. It was beautiful and poignant, but a complete sucker punch that I both love and hate Alden Bell for.

10/10 would recommend.

¡Qué chulada de libro! Aparte de pintarnos un precioso mundo típico de los libros postapocalípticos, nos da que pensar en la supervivencia y en las actuaciones de las personas en épocas de tensión. Interesantes personajes y bonita trama.

Reseña completa en YOGLAXX, blog de entretenimiento

Sinceramente no me esperaba nada de este libro, pense que iba ser aburrido pero decidi leermelo por que fue el regalo de unas amigas, asi que mi sorpresa fue muy grande, hay partes lentas y partes impresionantes y ahora me entero que hay segunda parte y no tengo idea de como lo continuaran asi que bueno, TENGO QUE LEERLO

I read this for my college class on zombie books and was pretty pleased with it overall. The main issue I had with it was that though it was beautifully written, it sometimes felt like the author was trying so hard to make it lovely that he sacrificed other necessary aspects of the book for that purpose. Despite that, the book is definitely worth reading.

It's been a busy summer and this book took me forever to finish.

It was pretty good...fearless girl...zombies.
I just couldn't deal with the fact that there isn't 1 "quotation" mark in the whole book...so that took getting used to.

Will read the other books in the series when I get a chance, but it's not a "OMG I have to read the next book Now" situation.

No cliffhanger, it just ends, unfortunately. It doesn't seem that the story continues on. I've read dozens of zombie books. Many have setting filler that you can skim through; however, you don't skip the filler here. You reread it. It's in both my zombies and distopian libraries. As for books go that truly make me feel, I haven't felt this way since I read "The Road".

This was incredible...the story of a "little girl" making do in the aftermath of your typical zombie apocalypse...but that's the only bit that's typical. The writing is sparse yet it's alive. This is one of the best books I've read this year...and so of course the library doesn't have the next one.

So many words, but nothing happens. I liked Temple, the main character. Hated the ending. The world and the plot have full of holes and inconsistencies in them. Maybe this book has some sort of deep meaning, but I can't get passed how dull it was. I found it a waste of time and I wish I had chosen another book.

A very strange zombie tale. Two gunslingers, one chasing the other to Texas where a "dummy" is supposed to find home. Strange tale. I'm sure I might have to read this again, it feels more psychological and spiritual than what I normally read. Not really about the zombies but what is good or evil in what a person chooses. Weird.

I read The Reapers Are the Angels quite a few years ago, but I remember exactly my feelings on it after I finished:

"That was badass."

I dug the southern-gothic style writing applied to a zombie apocalypse. I dug the tightly-woven adventure and action. And most of all, I loved the evolving dynamic between Temple and Moses.
Quick interesting read. Plot had huge holes, but the writing was great. Won't read on in the series... really liked Temple.

As it turns out, it is difficult for me to run across a book that I enjoyed so thoroughly as this one- and that makes me keep thinking about it more than a year after I read it out of sheer desire to remember what the characters were up to. So kudos Alden Bell- i think i docked a point for the weird sex scenes... dont understand why all southern gothic lit needs to have weird sex in it

I was worried that it would be too much of a zombie novel, but the zombies were pretty inconsequential. The book read really quickly. I liked Temple. I struggled with the "hand waving" over details like how the electrical grid was still working or that there was gasoline at the pumps. It made for a good discussion for my book club.
Solid vibes. Gave what it needed to give. No explanations. No expatiation.

This was a super unique take genre-wise for a zombie book, almost literary fiction in a post-apocalyptic world. There were some truly beautiful moments amidst the carnage typical of a zombie apocalypse. I really enjoyed it despite it not having any major blood-pumping scenes most zombie books are known for. I was very surprised by where the author took the ending.

I actually dropped it midway, I mean where the hell are captions, for crying out loud!! There was no captions, I couldn't guess who was talking and I couldn't even recognize that somebody was talking before I read the words 'she said' or 'he hissed'.
My god. Such a waste of money. Does Alden even know "" these exist??

Really an excellent little book. Starts out like a zombie novel but really becomes much more existential by the end. Very unique characters who struggle with maintaining some kind of moral compass in a zombie-infested world. A hard book to really do justice to in a review.

FANTASTIC book!!! I was drawn in from the very beginning and flipped through the pages as quickly as I could! This novel never slows down and keeps you interested from beginning to end.....and what a shocking end it is!!!
HIGHLY recommended!

Loved this book! It's hard to put down, and the character of Temple is one of the great tough heroines of fiction. I loved that this was a post-Apocalyptic book with hope and beauty. Seriously, do yourself a favor and read it!

A pretty good yarn here. Like The Road, something has gone dreadfully wrong, and now there are, well, zombies to contend with. Not a fantasy-type book, but good, solid science fiction. I found this book in a 'recommended by the librarians' bin at the library, and it was a great surprise

You know you have to read the book when ALL the jacket blurbs are by authors you like! Did not disappoint. Not the usual zombie apocalypse book in that the violence and survival are almost an afterthought to the human relationships in the story.

I really wanted to like this book ... but didn't. It just didn't ever seem all that convincing or intriguing. The characters seemed too cartoonish and the plot was kind of bland. Odd for a book that is set in the zombie apocalypse, but there you are.

This was the first zombie-type book I have ever read that I truly loved! The book is filled with action and heart (surprisingly). I definitely recommend it and I think it would make a great movie, too!

This felt like No Country for Old Men meets The Walking Dead. Loved it - especially the writer's choice of words and imagery throughout. Some scenes were ridiculously difficult to get through, but the whole thing was so compelling that I read this in a day.

What a great book. Temple was a terrific heroine. The zombies were wild. The story went a mile a minute. I hated the ending but I understood the why of it. The writing was gorgeous. It is one of those books that stays in your head for weeks after you finish it. I really enjoyed it.

I read this against my will. Geoff brought it home and I picked it up even though I knew I shouldn't! It was mixture of The Road and The Hunger Games. Way too violent & gory, plus sex and language--it had it all. Wish I could purge it. Dang!

I was home sick, and I sat down and read this in less than a day. Stark, to the point, about a girl born after the zombies had become, and places some rather stark reality on the whole issue. Not a happy ending, IMO, but all around a good book and worth my time.

Not your typical post-apocalypse zombie story! I loved the characters. At once amazing, hopeful, and depressing. The writing is incredible. It's the perfect combination of literature you expect to be assigned to read for English class, and zombie mayhem.

I thought I would like this more than I did. I was looking for creepy and exciting, but it really wasn't at all. It was a bit gory, but not scary. The story still kept me interested and the writing was great, it just wasn't what I was expecting.

This book is cliched and often poorly written. For a similar post-apocalyptic book with a strong female lead I recommend Far North instead. If zombies are your thing, well, read the Walking Dead or Robots Vs. Zombies.

From blog post

What if Flannery O'Connor had said to herself, "Screw it, I'm going to write a zombie novel"? The result might look something like Alden Bell's, The Reapers are the Angels.

Lovely zombie apocalypse. This is the story of young girl's fight to survive in a world that is miraculous and still beautiful even as mankind is fighting extinction. The proses are beautiful and the story powerful.

Gory, Gothic, poetical. I don't really like zombies or horror or lushly-vernacularly-written books, so I'm not this book's ideal reader: but I still got caught up in it. If you do like those things, definitely give it a try!

Zombie apocalypse novel for book groups -- not sure which group I would actually give this to but it is a dicussion worthy piece of literary fiction (with zombies). A 2011 Alex Award winner (adult books for YA)- definitely for the older teen due to content.

reminiscent of the heart wrenching depesperation of On the Road, this Zombie Apocolyptic tale isn't just about walking corpses. The horror and the beauty if what happens to people when we are stripped down to our barest forms, do we become in fact become the monsters? A great gritty read.

This book blew me away. It is hard to believe that a novel of this much beauty and depth is set during a zombie apocalypse. The hero Temple is one of the best written and developed characters I have read. I can not say enough good things about this novel.

didn't like this one:( couldn't really get into it at all and just felt bored mostly. last 50 or so pages definitely the best part but too little, too late. would not recommend, too many other great reads to spend your time on this one. huge let down:(

I unintentionally picked up a zombie book. I couldn't see the cover or what it was about so I was going by the title alone and thank god I was other wise I would have never picked up this book! It was not what I expected and I'm so happy i grabbed it.

I didn't love it but I liked it a whole lot. I enjoy badass female characters. There is a lot of gore and violence! After I read the last page, I laid Nook down on my stomach and thought about all I just read. I like books like that.

This book was a weird spin on zombie novels. It focuses more on the characters and their day to day rather than the zombies. I don't disagree with this idea for a novel but it just didn't overly do it for me. Still a pretty good read though.

Like Isaac Marion does with _Warm Bodies_, Bell proves that the 'zombie novel' can be so much more than a zombie novel:) Beautiful, lyrical and deeply moving,_The Reapers Are The Angels_ gave me the best kind of chills...

Thoughtful, well written - especially liked the author's use of words and even choice of names.
I can accept the hero dying - The event didn't make sense. Why would Moses take
Millie the mutant girl with him at all much less giving her access to a gun.
Anyway, other than that, good read.

I had to read this for an English project last year. So, naturally, I was skeptical about it. I was pleasantly surprised. This book is the BEST book I've read in a really long time. Great plot, great characters, just an all-around great book.

Who would have thought that I would find the character of a southern, female teenager in a post-apocalyptic America so philosophically deep and genuinely relatable. Temple makes this short book come alive with her unique voice and seen-it-all attitude.

What a ride!

This seemed like a mindless story about zombies, but I was completely surprised by the depth of this novel. There were several wonderful lines that prove Bell knows what he's doing. Thought provoking, entertaining, and touching . . . I'd recommend it to anyone.

Unbelievably good. My #1 book of the year, I'm pretty sure. It manages to do that rare thing of being beautifully written at the sentence/word level and also, plotwise, insanely gripping: I read it in one sitting. And what a heroine Temple is! Amazing, amazing.

i like the writing style and the word choices, the portrayal of dialect and the absence of quotation marks. i also like how it focuses on the beauty of the world after the apocolypse and thee constant battle of what is good. in my opinion temple is a reaper, and the reapers are the angels.

Wow! A powerful and different zombie book. Set far into the future of the zombie apocalypse. Temple kicks ass. Would take down any heroine I've read so far. I like that the author took risks in the ending.

FANTASTIC book! It was so fabulous I went out to find more by this author and there aren't any! Ok well there are 2 more but they aren't in this genre.

This really isn't a book about zombies. It's about people.
Meh. Yes, the writing is good, but I have to admit I got to the end and thought, "I stayed up late for this?" Undoubtedly a lack of literary sophistication, or possibly a lack of interest in zombies.

A surprise, how good this one is. One of the blurbs calls it "Flanner O'Connor with zombies," and that's totally accurate, only somehow doesn't put enough emphasis on the O'Connor part of the equation. It's Southern Gothic and it's great.

Reading a story about zombie apocalypse is not what I might choose first, but definitely a 10 for originality -- 10 for keeping me thinking about it -- 6 for violence -- 9 for character -- 7 for gory -- 9 for writing style. So, I think I am at an 8/10 or 4/5.

hmmmmm

What is wrong with this girl? You don't sleep beside strange men you just met after a guy tries to rape you! It doesn't matter if they told you they're not going to hurt you. I mean... talk about stupidity.

Post-Apocalyptic Zombie infested America with hints of The Road and Mad Max. The prose is as haunting as the setting and as visceral. The Zombies themselves are the least of the heroine's worries as she struggles to find purpose in a lost world.

Beautifully written, compelling, and something one rarely finds in zombie books - philosophical. This book is lovely and gruesome; Temple is a compelling character, as is Moses Todd. I spent half the book trying to figure out if I hated Moses or loved him and the end made it even harder to choose.

I appreciated the bleakness of the story. Refreshing and humanizing in it's endeavor to prove that the role of protagonist/antagonsit is relative to the perspective of the main character and the relationship between said character and the reader.

This was a really great take on the zobmie novel. A nice, pensive, looks at the post-apocalyptic world. The narrator was also excellent. I'm finding that I really like books that pull of younger narrators well.

Very different book. I loved the main character and the rapid pace of the book. Anything that mocks suburbia (where I live) is high on my list. Plus, it's got zombies in it. Doesn't get any better than that. Seriously, if this book doesn't make you look back over your life, you're made of stone.

I almost didn't read this one. After reading the back cover, I thought ; " Oh God no. Not another End of the World Zombie Book with a tough "Katniss" rip-off as the heroine. HOWEVER.........This is a touching beautiful book. Different from any other Post Apocalyptic book I've ever read. 5-STARS

I thought this was a fantastic read. The writing was very evocative, and I could really feel the story. I was actually growing anxious and sad as I approached the end if the book, knowing that it would soon be over. I highly recommend it.

I had a break of a couple years in between reading the first half and the second half of this book. The ending wasn't quite what I was expecting, but was still very satisfying. Some thought provoking ideas about fate.

Really enjoyed this book once I got used to the narrative. Not used to reading books written in that voice. But as much as I enjoyed the book- I hated the ending ten times as much. Total let down. Hated the ending, but would still recommend the book.

This book is really something else. At first it started off boring, but once i got to the middle it was like wow! This book isn't like everyother book on zombies. It's almost unbelievable. Overall it's a good book.

This book was amazing and so incredibly well written. I could really see the settings in my mind, which is something I seem to have a problem with in a lot of dystopian or post apocalyptic fiction I've been reading. Everything jumps off the page here. Really well done and absolutely devasting.

I don't know why I waited so long to read this. I mean, this right here, is a treasure. A treasure of words and feelings and tears and happiness. What a beautifully written book about a girl surviving in a world of darkness and death...the only world she has ever known.

I haven't read many zombie books, but this one so far is my favorite. The whole story felt so real, like it could really happen, or such a place exists today. And Temple was the perfect narrator for it.

Recommendation from a friend - post-apocalyptic zombie infested world, but with a young girl as the protagonist and heroine. I like the way the dialogue is written, without quotations and just filled in throughout the book, so you have to pay attention.

SO GOOD. The writing style--deep and detailed without arousing headaches. The plot somehow manages to be thrilling even though most of it involves Temple just thinking. Her thinking--really thought-evoking in general.

New favorite book.

If you only read one ( or two) zombie books in your lifetime, this should be the one to read! Sort of reminded me of Blood Red Road, but with the undead. Strong female protagonist, literary details and language.

There is a lot going on in this "literary" version of the zombie novel. Not sure how much is actually there vs just the appearance, but I enjoyed it at any rate. Walker Percy/Flannery O'Connor + zombies = win. Just not sure if that's "win" or "WIN."

Zombies aren't really my thing, but this is a nicely done literary horror story of a world taken over by "meatheads" with a great main character written in a similar vein as Cormac McCarthy's The Road.

well..i liked it..the zombies arent the main "enemy" in the book but im not sure how i felt about the ending it seemed rather anti-climactic..**spoiler ahead** i didnt think temple would survive but i also didnt expect her to have/meet the ending she did..

Worst title ever, but a surprisingly excellent book. Zombie genre fiction with a solid Southern Gothic ethos. Upsetting, satisfying and not a hint of pandering. Well written, and Temple is an unforgettable character.

Send to Morgan?

I read an ARC edition and I loved it all the way up to the ending...then that's when I didn't like it so much anymore. Temple is pretty bad-ass and very independent, which I appreciated, then again, the ending happened and ruined the whole book for me :(

Mixed feelings on this book. Loved the first 98% of it, not so much the last 2%. I give the first 98% 5 stars, and 0 stars for the last 2%, for an overall rating of 3 stars. I'll probably still read the second book in the series, just not anytime soon.

This is the story of Temple, a young girl who is making her way in an apocalyptic, zombified landscape. Most obviously, her goal is to survive. Along the way she attempts to address questions about the world she lives in and her place within this world
I was very surprised at how good this book actually was. Having never read anything by this author, and usually finding the whole "zombie" thing too cheesy, I was sceptical. Alden Bell made it work.

I loved this book. Zombies are all the rage, but this stands above in my opinion. What a heroine. What a story. I write this several months after finishing the book, and it stands out above the other novels I've read this year. I'm looking for more by Alden Bell.

i feel really good about the zombie apocalypse after listening to this book, which is less about zombies than you'd think. actually, the zombies aren't even the scariest characters, they're manageable.

A thoughtful, well written different take on the whole zombie genere, sad, exciting and a good read.
